rules.title: Code simplification
rules.prompt: Check whether the changed code can be simplified without weakening behavior, validation, or diagnostics.

rules.title: Project style fit
rules.prompt: Check whether the change follows the local project style, naming, module boundaries, and existing helper patterns.

rules.title: Unnecessary abstraction
rules.prompt: Check whether the change introduced abstractions that do not remove real duplication, risk, or complexity.

rules.title: Class/function/file growth
rules.prompt: Check whether touched classes, functions, or files grew enough to need local extraction or clearer ownership.

rules.title: Hardcoded values and contracts
rules.prompt: Check whether new literals, paths, statuses, or messages should be named constants, schema fields, or shared contracts.

rules.title: Duplicated logic and contracts
rules.prompt: Check whether the change duplicates logic, validation, or contract strings that should stay defined in one place.

rules.title: Test and verification scope
rules.prompt: Check whether the focused tests and mandatory gates cover the behavioral risk without adding unrelated slow coverage.

rules.title: Ops shell strict error handling
rules.prompt: For shell or ops-script changes, check strict shell behavior, error propagation, exit-code handling, traps or cleanup paths, and cross-shell or platform portability.

rules.title: Ops deploy and backup idempotency
rules.prompt: For deploy, backup, restore, or operations scripts, check idempotency, safe retries, dry-run or confirmation semantics, rollback or cleanup behavior, and restore verification where backup data is involved.

rules.title: Ops secrets and environment loading
rules.prompt: For shell or ops changes, check secret handling, log redaction, env-file loading safety, and whether duplicated environment-loading snippets should reuse or extract a shared helper.

rules.title: Trust-boundary and adversarial-path analysis
rules.prompt: For security, authorization, protected-control-plane, recovery, evidence, or artifact-trust changes, provide a compact trust_boundary_matrix. Name every trust boundary and record its authority source, mutable inputs, immutable or integrity-bound evidence, canonical reconstruction, TOCTOU or replay behavior, and targeted negative paths with test evidence. Every negative-path evidence_files entry must use path#exact test name, scenario must equal that declared test name, and the named test callback must contain a direct assertion statement outside conditional control flow or a nested callback. Happy-path evidence alone is not sufficient.
